dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvasrotonibandhena prāṇaśaktyordhvayā śanaiḥ | pipīlasparśavelāyām prathate paramaṃ sukham ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When all the streams (of the senses) are blocked and the breath-power rises slowly upward, at the moment of a sensation like ants creeping, supreme happiness spreads.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: when the openings of all the senses are stopped and the mind is thought-free, prāṇaśakti rises in the central channel, felt as an ant-like tingling at the stations it passes, and supreme delight follows. Singh records that Śivopādhyāya says the rise is achieved by breath retention (kumbhaka), and calls that quotation irrelevant. Wallis: stopping all the streams of prāṇa from flowing out through the senses and orifices.
dharana.technique_name: All Streams Closed, the Creeping of Ants
dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class. For practice, use Door 042.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 67 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: all sense openings (closed, in the classical method)
the breath-power rising along the central line
tingling like ants (at the stations it passes)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The classical map is the senses closed and a slow tingling rising up the central line. Drawn faint: studied, not drilled.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint vertical line with small dots rising along it, drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Rising tingle (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: energy that usually streams out through the senses is pictured turning inward and rising. A picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; let the body simply rest while you do
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: energy turned inward, felt as a rising tingle
attention.secondary: If sitting with anything, only gentle, ordinary body sensation

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When all the streams (of the senses) are blocked and the breath-power rises slowly upward, at the moment of a sensation like ants creeping, supreme happiness spreads.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: all the sense openings are closed and the breath-power rises slowly upward through the central channel; at the moment of an ant-like creeping sensation, supreme happiness spreads. Observe-only in this school: read and understand it. For practice, use Door 042.

honesty.disclosure: Door 044 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 44 (verse 67) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 044 is dharana 44, verse 67. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

historical/observe_only: The classical method closes all the sense openings (in commentary, by a sensory seal and breath retention) to make the breath-power rise; this school does not teach sense-sealing or retention. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Sensory sealing and breath retention are not taught by this school. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
safety.observe_only_note: Observe-only. Closing the sense openings and holding the breath can bring dizziness, panic or fainting and is not suitable for everyone. For practice, use Door 042 or a gentle body-sensation door.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 044: all streams closed, the creeping of ants. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 44, verse 67. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make, and no drill. Sit comfortably while we read. Its classical map is the senses closed and a tingling rising up the centre.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body rest completely. Eyes open, reading or resting softly. Attention on understanding, not on doing.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. Nothing to practise with the breath here. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the idea, not the method: energy that streams out through the senses can be pictured turning inward and rising.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: outflowing energy turning inward. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 67: describes blocking all the streams of the senses, the breath-power rising slowly, and supreme happiness at a feeling like creeping ants. Observe-only here. For practice, use Door 042.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Close the text. Take a normal breath. Look around the room and move on when ready.
